memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Lord God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep; and while he was sleeping, he took one of the man's ribs and then closed up the place with flesh. Then the Lord God made a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man. — Gen 2:21–22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is such gentleness in this scene. God causes the man to fall into a deep sleep—Adam does nothing, contributes nothing, simply rests while God works. The greatest gift in his life is being prepared while he is completely unaware. How often God is at work for us in ways we cannot see, quietly arranging good things while we rest in His care.

Then notice how the woman is made. God does not form her separately from the dust, as He did the man. He takes her from the man's own side. The old teachers noticed the beauty in this: she was not taken from his head to rule over him, nor from his feet to be trampled by him, but from his side—to stand beside him as an equal, near his heart to be loved. Man and woman share the same nature, the same worth, the same dignity before God. Both bear His image (Gen 1:27).

And God "brought her to the man." The Lord Himself is the one who gives, the giver of every good relationship. What God provides, He provides personally and with love.

This picture of a bride, formed and brought to her husband, echoes gently through all of Scripture. Christ is the bridegroom who gave Himself for His bride, the church, cleansing her and one day presenting her to Himself (Eph 5:25–27). The care God showed in Eden points us to the greater love of Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where might God be quietly working for your good, even while you cannot see it?
- Do you treat others as equals made in God's image, worthy of dignity and love?
- How does Christ's love for His bride, the church, move your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You for the tender care with which You make and give good things. Help me to rest in Your unseen work, to honour others as image-bearers, and to treasure the love of Christ for His people. Amen.
